what_it_is: A set-off cancels what a party owes you against what you owe them. No money moves — only the difference stays outstanding.
two_ledgers_hint: A party who both buys from you and sells to you has two accounts, one customer and one supplier, because a single balance cannot be both a receivable and a payable. This document is the bridge between them.
most_that_can_be_offset: The most that can be set off is {amount} — the smaller of the two sides.
exceeds_overlap: That is more than one of the two sides holds. A set-off can only cover the overlap.
pick_both_accounts: Choose a customer account and a supplier account to see what can be set off.
nothing_to_offset: There is nothing to set off: one of the two sides has no outstanding balance.
same_party_hint: These two accounts should belong to the same person or company.
leave_empty_for_oldest_first: Leave the selection empty to apply the amount oldest-first.
one_currency_only: Both sides must be in the same currency. Offsetting across currencies is a currency trade as well as a set-off, and the rate it happens at is a commercial agreement.
reverse_hint: Both halves are reversed together. Reversing one side alone would relieve one party of a debt the other still carries.
no_edit_hint: A posted set-off is not edited. Reverse it and enter the correct one — both parties agreed to what was posted.
clearing_is_square: The two halves cancelled: nothing is left in clearing.
pairing_hint: Only if this is the same person or company trading both ways. Leave empty otherwise.
nothing_overlaps: Nothing overlaps right now — one side has no outstanding balance.
also_trades_the_other_way: This party also has a {role} account with {amount} outstanding. A set-off may be cheaper than moving money.
